finding: The delta made the two red-then-green exits of step 4 and step 6 restore the step 3 fix before returning `blocked`, but a third `blocked` exit can fire on the same reverted run and still leaves the fix out. The test that step 4 adds at a live tier runs first with the fix reverted, under "Live tiers". When the caller handed over no instance or no restart command, "Live tiers" returns `blocked` at that point, and nothing says to restore the fix first. The same applies to a live scenario in step 6.
why: Delta-sweep item: "a fix applied at one site while a sibling path keeps the old behaviour" (skills/afk/review/checklists/delta-sweep.md:8). The procedure's record rule says `blocked` keeps the fix in the tree: skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:218-219 "`fail`, `adversary_fail` and `blocked` leave the edits made so far, listed under Edits." On this path the Edits field names a fix that is no longer in the working tree.
fix: State the restore once, for every exit: "Any return while the step 3 fix is reverted (step 4, step 6, or the Live tiers rule) restores the fix first." Alternatively, check in step 4 and step 6 that the instance and the restart command were handed over before reverting the fix.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:115-119 "Watch each test this step adds fail with the step 3 fix reverted, then pass with it restored; the record holds both runs. A live-tier test follows "Live tiers" for each of the two runs. An added test that passes with the fix reverted, or fails with it restored → restore the step 3 fix, then return `blocked`, naming the test."; skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:43-46 "A check that runs against the running instance runs, in any step, only after the caller's restart command has restarted that instance on the current working tree. A live check with no instance or no restart command handed over → return `blocked`, naming the check."; skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:156-157 "A scenario escape analysis fixes in place that does not go red, then green → restore the step 3 fix, then return `blocked`, naming the scenario."; skills/afk/fix/SKILL.md:14 "with none, a live tier ends the procedure `blocked`." Method: I searched the slice files for `blocked` and `restore` and read every `blocked` exit that can fire while the fix is reverted.

finding: The new two-way-door branch in Phase 1 records the wrong binding SDD decision in plan/DECISIONS.md, applies it, and later Phase 3 runs procedure step 7, which classifies the same frozen-SDD change again and records it again. Example: a feature-session V-3 whose cause is a wrong SDD section 8 decision, classified a two-way door, ends with two ledger entries (D-n at Phase 1, D-n+1 at Phase 3) for one fork.
why: DECISIONS.md:52 "a new fork on the same ground gets a new entry" covers only a new fork, and the ledger is append-only (DECISIONS.md:35 "Append-only: never edit or delete a prior entry"), so the duplicate cannot be removed; the human's end-of-run audit (DECISIONS.md:53) lists the same decision twice.
fix: In IN-PLACE-FIX.md step 7, record a two-way door only when plan/DECISIONS.md holds no entry for that decision yet (an existing entry: put its D-id into the record), or have fix Phase 3 hand step 7 the D-id Phase 1 recorded.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/SKILL.md:37 "A two-way door → record it per `DECISIONS.md` and go to step 3, with the recorded decision as the Fix proposal."; skills/afk/fix/SKILL.md:57 "Run [IN-PLACE-FIX.md](IN-PLACE-FIX.md) step 7"; skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:176-178 "Classify a change to a frozen SDD decision by `DECISIONS.md` as in step 3: a one-way door or a tie → run step 8, then return `design_conflict`; a two-way door is recorded, and the SDD goes into the record as stale."

finding: Fixed key f069 made step 3's one-way-door branch put the SDD or ADR into the record as a stale artifact before it runs step 8, so step 8's skip rule (no miss class and no stale artifact) cannot drop the lesson.
